cases.sentence: Ты вот смотришь на этих старичков, – сказал он, указывая на сгорбленного члена с отвислою губой, который, чуть передвигая ноги в ___, прошел им навстречу, – и думаешь, что они так родились шлюпиками.
cases.explain: «мягких сапогах» — after the preposition «в», for location or topic.
cases.translation: “Yes, it’s interesting for you. But its interest for me is quite different. You look at those little old men now,” he said, pointing to a club member with bent back and projecting lip, shuffling towards them in his soft boots, “and imagine that they were shlupiks like that from their birth up.”

cases.sentence: Стараясь не шуметь, они вошли и в темную читальную, где под лампами с абажурами сидел один ___ с сердитым лицом, перехватывавший один журнал за другим, и плешивый генерал, углубленный в чтение.
cases.explain: «молодой человек» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: Talking and greeting the friends they met, Levin and the prince walked through all the rooms: the great room where tables had already been set, and the usual partners were playing for small stakes; the divan room, where they were playing chess, and Sergey Ivanovitch was sitting talking to somebody; the billiard room, where, about a sofa in a recess, there was a lively party drinking champagne—Gagin was one of them. They peeped into the “infernal regions,” where a good many men were crowding round one table, at which Yashvin was sitting. Trying not to make a noise, they walked into the dark reading room, where under the shaded lamps there sat a young man with a wrathful countenance, turning over one journal after another, and a bald general buried in a book. They went, too, into what the prince called the intellectual room, where three gentlemen were engaged in a heated discussion of the latest political news.

cases.sentence: Левин посидел, послушал; но, вспомнив все разговоры ___, ему вдруг стало ужасно скучно.
cases.explain: «нынешнего утра» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Prince, please come, we’re ready,” said one of his card party, who had come to look for him, and the prince went off. Levin sat down and listened, but recalling all the conversation of the morning he felt all of a sudden fearfully bored. He got up hurriedly, and went to look for Oblonsky and Turovtsin, with whom it had been so pleasant.

cases.sentence: Туровцын сидел с кружкой питья на ___ в бильярдной, и Степан Аркадьич с Вронским о чем-то разговаривали у двери в дальнем углу комнаты.
cases.explain: «высоком диване» — after the preposition «на», for location or topic.
cases.translation: Turovtsin was one of the circle drinking in the billiard room, and Stepan Arkadyevitch was talking with Vronsky near the door at the farther corner of the room.

cases.sentence: И я хочу и знаю, что вы должны быть дружны и близки, потому что вы оба ___.
cases.explain: «хорошие люди» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: “This is a true friend of mine—almost my greatest friend,” he said to Vronsky. “You have become even closer and dearer to me. And I want you, and I know you ought, to be friends, and great friends, because you’re both splendid fellows.”

cases.sentence: Но, несмотря на желание Степана Аркадьича и их ___, им говорить было нечего, и оба это чувствовали.
cases.explain: «взаимное желание» — the subject of the sentence stands in the nominative.
cases.translation: But in spite of Stepan Arkadyevitch’s desire, and their own desire, they had nothing to talk about, and both felt it.

cases.sentence: Левин испытывал ___ от умственной усталости утра.
cases.explain: «приятный отдых» — the accusative marks the direct object of the verb.
cases.translation: After the game Vronsky and Levin sat down at Gagin’s table, and at Stepan Arkadyevitch’s suggestion Levin took a hand in the game. Vronsky sat down at the table, surrounded by friends, who were incessantly coming up to him. Every now and then he went to the “infernal” to keep an eye on Yashvin. Levin was enjoying a delightful sense of repose after the mental fatigue of the morning. He was glad that all hostility was at an end with Vronsky, and the sense of peace, decorum, and comfort never left him.

cases.explain: «сельского хозяйства» — the genitive here marks possession, absence, or quantity.
cases.translation: “Oh, nowhere specially. I promised Sviazhsky to go to the Society of Agriculture. By all means, let us go,” said Levin.
